primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Glomerulotubular balance mediated partly by proximal-tubule flow sensing
mechanism: When single-nephron filtration and proximal luminal flow increase, absolute proximal sodium and bicarbonate reabsorption rises so that fractional reabsorption remains relatively stable. Proximal-tubule brush-border microvilli act as flow sensors; increased shear/torque promotes NHE3 trafficking and transport activity, coupling tubular reabsorption to filtered load.
vignette: In an experimental preparation, single-nephron glomerular filtration rate is increased while plasma hormone concentrations and systemic blood pressure are held constant. Absolute proximal sodium and bicarbonate reabsorption increase, but the fraction of the filtered load reabsorbed in the proximal tubule remains nearly unchanged.
lead: Which cellular response most directly contributes to this adaptation?
correct: Flow-induced recruitment and activation of apical Na+/H+ exchanger 3 in proximal tubular cells
distractors: Flow-induced internalization of apical Na+/H+ exchanger 3 in proximal tubular cells
Increased insertion of epithelial sodium channels into proximal tubular brush-border membranes
Reduced basolateral Na+/K+-ATPase activity in proximal tubular cells
Increased vasopressin-dependent aquaporin-2 insertion in proximal tubular cells
distractor_notes: Internalization of NHE3 would reduce proximal sodium and bicarbonate reabsorption rather than support glomerulotubular balance during increased flow.
ENaC is a distal-nephron epithelial sodium channel and is not the principal apical sodium-entry pathway mediating flow-dependent proximal reabsorption.
Reduced basolateral Na+/K+-ATPase activity would impair, not increase, transcellular proximal sodium transport.
AQP2 is vasopressin regulated in collecting-duct principal cells rather than the proximal tubule and does not mediate glomerulotubular balance.
key_expl: Glomerulotubular balance keeps proximal fractional reabsorption relatively constant when filtered load changes. Increased proximal luminal flow is sensed by brush-border microvilli and stimulates NHE3 trafficking/activity and other transport processes, increasing absolute sodium and bicarbonate reabsorption.
objective: Explain glomerulotubular balance as a flow-dependent proximal-tubule adaptation involving brush-border mechanosensing and increased NHE3-mediated transport.

outline: Low maternal unconjugated estriol and X-linked ichthyosis
primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
diagnosis: Placental steroid sulfatase deficiency causing X-linked ichthyosis
mechanism: Placental steroid sulfatase converts sulfated steroid precursors such as DHEAS to unconjugated forms used in placental estrogen synthesis. STS deficiency reduces maternal unconjugated estriol during pregnancy and causes X-linked ichthyosis in affected male offspring; delayed or abnormal labor can occur.
vignette: A 29-year-old pregnant woman has a 46,XY fetus. Second-trimester screening repeatedly shows a profoundly low maternal unconjugated estriol concentration, while fetal growth and anatomy are otherwise normal. Her brother and maternal uncle developed dark, polygonal scaling of the skin during infancy.
lead: Deficiency of which placental enzyme best explains these findings?
distractors: Aromatase
21-hydroxylase
11-beta-hydroxylase
5-alpha-reductase type 2
distractor_notes: Placental aromatase deficiency causes androgen accumulation and can virilize the mother and a 46,XX fetus; that phenotype is not described here.
21-hydroxylase deficiency causes congenital adrenal hyperplasia with abnormal adrenal steroid synthesis, not the X-linked ichthyosis/very-low-uE3 pattern.
11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency causes androgen excess and mineralocorticoid effects rather than isolated low maternal unconjugated estriol with an X-linked skin disorder.
5-alpha-reductase type 2 deficiency impairs conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone and causes undervirilization in 46,XY individuals, not placental estriol deficiency.
key_expl: Very low maternal unconjugated estriol with a male fetus and maternal-line male relatives with X-linked ichthyosis is classic for placental steroid sulfatase deficiency. Loss of STS impairs conversion of sulfated steroid precursors needed for placental estriol synthesis.
objective: Recognize placental steroid sulfatase deficiency from very low maternal unconjugated estriol and an X-linked family history of ichthyosis.
clues: affected maternal-line male relatives with polygonal scaling

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Mitochondrial HMG-CoA lyase cleaves HMG-CoA to acetoacetate and acetyl-CoA, a required step in ketogenesis and a step in leucine catabolism. Deficiency produces inability to generate adequate ketone bodies during fasting or illness, causing hypoketotic hypoglycemia, metabolic acidosis, and characteristic organic aciduria.
vignette: An 8-month-old infant becomes lethargic and vomits during a viral illness with poor oral intake. Laboratory studies show hypoglycemia, metabolic acidosis, and very low serum ketones. Urine organic acid analysis shows increased 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaric and 3-methylglutaric acids.
lead: Deficiency of which enzyme most directly explains this presentation?
distractors: Medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase
Propionyl-CoA carboxylase
Methylmalonyl-CoA mutase
Branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase
distractor_notes: MCAD deficiency also causes hypoketotic hypoglycemia during fasting but has a different acylcarnitine/organic-acid pattern and does not cause the characteristic HMG-related metabolites.
Propionyl-CoA carboxylase deficiency causes propionic acidemia with organic acid accumulation and hyperammonemia but not the HMG-CoA lyase metabolite pattern.
Methylmalonyl-CoA mutase deficiency causes methylmalonic acidemia and does not specifically block ketone-body formation from HMG-CoA.
Branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase deficiency causes maple syrup urine disease with elevated branched-chain amino acids and ketoacids.
key_expl: The combination of fasting-triggered hypoketotic hypoglycemia and urinary 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaric/3-methylglutaric acids identifies HMG-CoA lyase deficiency. The enzyme is required for formation of acetoacetate during ketogenesis.
objective: Connect hypoketotic hypoglycemia with characteristic HMG-related organic acids to HMG-CoA lyase deficiency and impaired ketogenesis.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Primary iron loading in non-transfusion-dependent beta-thalassemia from hepcidin suppression
mechanism: In beta-thalassemia, ineffective erythropoiesis expands erythroid precursors and increases erythroferrone production. Erythroferrone suppresses hepatic hepcidin despite iron loading, preserving ferroportin activity and increasing intestinal iron absorption and iron release from stores. This can cause clinically important iron overload even without regular transfusions.
vignette: A 26-year-old man with non-transfusion-dependent beta-thalassemia develops progressively increasing liver iron concentration despite receiving no regular red blood cell transfusions. He has marked erythroid marrow expansion and elevated erythropoietin.
lead: Which signaling change most directly promotes this patient's progressive iron loading?
correct: Increased erythroferrone production with suppression of hepatic hepcidin
distractors: Decreased erythroferrone production with increased hepatic hepcidin
Increased hepcidin binding to ferroportin with enhanced intestinal iron uptake
Reduced ferroportin expression on enterocytes due to absent erythropoietic drive
Increased hepcidin synthesis caused directly by expanded erythroid precursors
distractor_notes: Ineffective erythropoiesis increases, rather than decreases, erythroferrone signaling and produces inappropriately low hepcidin relative to iron burden.
Hepcidin binding causes ferroportin internalization and reduces iron export/absorption; it would oppose, not promote, iron loading.
Erythroid expansion increases signals that maintain iron availability; reduced ferroportin would decrease systemic iron entry.
Expanded erythropoiesis suppresses hepcidin through erythroid-derived regulators such as erythroferrone rather than directly increasing hepcidin synthesis.
key_expl: Non-transfusion-dependent beta-thalassemia can cause primary iron overload because ineffective erythropoiesis increases erythroferrone, which suppresses hepcidin. Low hepcidin maintains ferroportin-mediated iron export from enterocytes and stores, increasing systemic iron.
objective: Explain iron overload in non-transfusion-dependent beta-thalassemia through the erythroferrone-hepcidin-ferroportin axis.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Systemic-capillary chloride shift during carbon dioxide transport
mechanism: In systemic tissues, carbon dioxide enters erythrocytes and is rapidly converted by carbonic anhydrase to bicarbonate and hydrogen ions. Bicarbonate leaves the erythrocyte in exchange for chloride through the HCO3-/Cl- exchanger, allowing most carbon dioxide to be transported in plasma as bicarbonate while maintaining electroneutrality.
vignette: As blood traverses systemic capillaries in metabolically active skeletal muscle, carbon dioxide diffuses into erythrocytes and is rapidly hydrated by carbonic anhydrase. Most of the resulting carbon dioxide load is ultimately carried in plasma as bicarbonate.
lead: Which transmembrane ion movement normally facilitates this process at the tissue level?
correct: Bicarbonate exits the erythrocyte while chloride enters
distractors: Bicarbonate enters the erythrocyte while chloride exits
Hydrogen ions exit the erythrocyte in exchange for sodium
Chloride exits the erythrocyte in exchange for potassium
Bicarbonate and chloride enter the erythrocyte together through a cotransporter
distractor_notes: This is the direction favored in pulmonary capillaries when the chloride shift reverses to regenerate carbon dioxide for exhalation.
Hydrogen ions generated from carbonic acid are largely buffered by deoxygenated hemoglobin rather than exported through a sodium-hydrogen exchanger as the key CO2-transport step.
A chloride-potassium exchanger is not the mechanism responsible for conversion of tissue CO2 into plasma bicarbonate.
The erythrocyte band-3 pathway is an electroneutral bicarbonate-chloride exchanger, not a cotransporter moving both ions in the same direction.
key_expl: At systemic capillaries, intracellular carbonic anhydrase converts CO2 to bicarbonate and H+. Bicarbonate exits RBCs in exchange for chloride through band 3/AE1; this chloride shift permits large-scale transport of CO2 as plasma bicarbonate.
objective: Describe the direction of the erythrocyte chloride shift in systemic tissues and its role in carbon dioxide transport.
clues: most CO2 carried as plasma bicarbonate

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: During intense exercise, skeletal muscle regenerates cytosolic NAD+ by reducing pyruvate to lactate. Lactate enters the circulation and is taken up by the liver, where lactate dehydrogenase regenerates pyruvate and gluconeogenesis converts it to glucose. The glucose can return to muscle, transferring part of the energetic burden of anaerobic metabolism to the liver.
vignette: During repeated all-out sprints, a healthy athlete relies heavily on anaerobic glycolysis in skeletal muscle. Lactate released from the working muscle is taken up by the liver and later contributes to restoration of circulating glucose available to the muscle.
lead: Which hepatic process is most directly responsible for recycling this lactate?
correct: Conversion of lactate to pyruvate followed by gluconeogenesis
distractors: Conversion of lactate to acetyl-CoA followed by ketogenesis
Direct polymerization of lactate into glycogen
Conversion of lactate to alanine followed by ureagenesis
Oxidation of lactate to carbon dioxide without formation of glucose
distractor_notes: Lactate is first converted to pyruvate; acetyl-CoA cannot provide net carbon for gluconeogenesis and ketogenesis does not regenerate circulating glucose for the muscle.
Lactate is not directly incorporated into glycogen; it must first be converted to pyruvate and then to glucose through gluconeogenesis.
The glucose-alanine cycle involves amino-group transfer and alanine transport from muscle to liver, whereas the vignette specifically describes lactate recycling.
The defining Cori-cycle function is hepatic regeneration of glucose from lactate, not merely oxidative disposal of lactate.
key_expl: The Cori cycle transfers lactate produced by anaerobic glycolysis in working muscle to the liver. Hepatic lactate dehydrogenase converts lactate back to pyruvate, which enters gluconeogenesis to form glucose that can return to muscle.
objective: Explain the Cori cycle as hepatic conversion of skeletal-muscle lactate to glucose through lactate dehydrogenase and gluconeogenesis.

diagnosis: Violation of the exclusion-restriction assumption in Mendelian randomization
mechanism: Mendelian randomization uses genetic variants as instrumental variables for an exposure. A valid instrument must associate with the exposure, be independent of exposure-outcome confounders, and affect the outcome only through the exposure. A direct pathway from the variant to the outcome that bypasses the exposure is horizontal pleiotropy and violates the exclusion restriction.
vignette: Investigators use a genetic variant associated with lifelong lower LDL cholesterol as an instrumental variable to estimate the causal effect of LDL cholesterol on myocardial infarction. Further studies show that the same variant also directly reduces vascular inflammation through a pathway that does not involve LDL cholesterol.
lead: Which assumption required for a valid Mendelian-randomization estimate is most directly violated?
correct: The genetic instrument affects the outcome only through the exposure of interest
distractors: The genetic instrument is associated with the exposure of interest
The outcome must be measured before the exposure
The exposure must be normally distributed in the source population
The genetic instrument must explain all variation in the exposure
distractor_notes: Association between the genetic instrument and the exposure is a required relevance condition and is explicitly present here.
Mendelian randomization does not require the outcome to precede the exposure; the causal direction under study is from exposure to outcome.
Normality of the exposure distribution is not a core instrumental-variable validity assumption.
An instrument need not explain all exposure variance; it must be sufficiently associated with the exposure and satisfy the independence/exclusion assumptions.
key_expl: The variant has a direct LDL-independent effect on vascular inflammation and therefore on myocardial infarction risk. This horizontal pleiotropy violates the exclusion restriction: the instrument must affect the outcome only through the exposure being instrumented.
objective: Recognize horizontal pleiotropy as a violation of the exclusion-restriction assumption in Mendelian randomization.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Plasma pseudocholinesterase/butyrylcholinesterase, encoded by BCHE and produced largely in the liver, hydrolyzes succinylcholine and mivacurium. Inherited low-activity variants cause markedly prolonged neuromuscular paralysis after standard succinylcholine exposure. A low dibucaine number indicates an atypical enzyme that is relatively resistant to dibucaine inhibition.
vignette: A previously healthy 31-year-old woman receives succinylcholine during induction of general anesthesia. The surgery is brief, but she remains flaccid and apneic for several hours despite being awake when sedation is lightened. Electrolytes, temperature, and acid-base status are normal. A dibucaine inhibition test shows markedly reduced inhibition of plasma cholinesterase activity.
lead: Which diagnosis best explains the prolonged paralysis?
distractors: Malignant hyperthermia
Myasthenia gravis
Organophosphate poisoning
Hyperkalemic periodic paralysis
distractor_notes: Malignant hyperthermia causes hypermetabolism, hypercarbia, rigidity, hyperthermia, and acidosis rather than isolated prolonged succinylcholine paralysis with an abnormal dibucaine test.
Myasthenia gravis alters neuromuscular transmission but does not produce the characteristic low dibucaine inhibition phenotype.
Organophosphate poisoning causes cholinergic excess with muscarinic and nicotinic manifestations rather than isolated post-succinylcholine paralysis in an otherwise healthy patient.
Hyperkalemic periodic paralysis is associated with episodic weakness and hyperkalemia, not a pharmacogenetic defect in succinylcholine hydrolysis.
key_expl: Prolonged paralysis after succinylcholine with a low dibucaine number is classic for inherited pseudocholinesterase deficiency. Atypical BCHE variants hydrolyze succinylcholine poorly and are less inhibited by dibucaine than normal enzyme.
objective: Recognize inherited pseudocholinesterase deficiency from prolonged succinylcholine paralysis and an abnormal dibucaine inhibition test.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: During fasting, glucagon raises hepatocyte cAMP and activates protein kinase A. In liver, PKA phosphorylates the bifunctional PFK-2/FBPase-2 enzyme, decreasing its kinase activity and favoring its phosphatase activity. Fructose-2,6-bisphosphate falls, reducing PFK-1 activity and relieving inhibition of fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase, thereby suppressing glycolysis and favoring gluconeogenesis.
vignette: A healthy man has fasted overnight. Hepatic glucagon signaling increases cAMP and protein kinase A activity. The liver shifts away from glycolysis and toward gluconeogenesis despite adequate supplies of gluconeogenic substrate.
lead: Which change in a key allosteric regulator most directly contributes to this metabolic shift?
distractors: Increased fructose-2,6-bisphosphate concentration
Increased AMP concentration as the primary glucagon signal
Decreased acetyl-CoA concentration
Increased fructose-1,6-bisphosphate concentration caused by direct PFK-1 activation
distractor_notes: Fructose-2,6-bisphosphate activates PFK-1 and inhibits fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase; increasing it would favor glycolysis rather than fasting-state gluconeogenesis.
Glucagon signals through cAMP/PKA, not by increasing AMP as the primary regulatory signal; AMP also tends to favor PFK-1 and inhibit fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase.
During fasting, fatty-acid oxidation increases hepatic acetyl-CoA, which supports gluconeogenesis by activating pyruvate carboxylase.
Glucagon lowers fructose-2,6-bisphosphate and decreases PFK-1 activity; direct PFK-1 activation would oppose the fasting-state shift.
key_expl: Glucagon-activated PKA phosphorylates hepatic PFK-2/FBPase-2, lowering fructose-2,6-bisphosphate. This decreases PFK-1 activity and releases fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase from inhibition, shifting hepatic flux from glycolysis toward gluconeogenesis.
objective: Explain how glucagon lowers hepatic fructose-2,6-bisphosphate to reciprocally regulate glycolysis and gluconeogenesis during fasting.

outline: Reduced 2,3-BPG binding and increased oxygen affinity
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: High oxygen affinity of fetal hemoglobin due to reduced 2,3-BPG binding
mechanism: Fetal hemoglobin is alpha2gamma2. Its gamma chains bind 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate less avidly than the beta chains of adult hemoglobin. Reduced 2,3-BPG binding stabilizes the high-affinity state, left-shifting the fetal oxygen dissociation curve and facilitating transfer of oxygen from maternal to fetal blood across the placenta.
vignette: Maternal and fetal blood flow through the placenta in close proximity without mixing. At the same oxygen partial pressure, fetal erythrocytes maintain a higher hemoglobin oxygen saturation than maternal erythrocytes.
lead: Which molecular property of fetal hemoglobin most directly accounts for this difference?
correct: Reduced binding of 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate to gamma globin chains
distractors: Increased binding of 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate to gamma globin chains
Reduced cooperativity among the four heme groups
Replacement of alpha globin chains by gamma globin chains
Increased affinity of fetal hemoglobin for carbon dioxide
distractor_notes: Greater 2,3-BPG binding would stabilize the low-affinity deoxygenated state and shift the curve to the right, opposite the fetal phenotype.
The key physiologic difference is the allosteric effect of reduced 2,3-BPG binding; impaired cooperativity is not the normal mechanism enabling fetal oxygen uptake.
HbF contains the same alpha chains as HbA; beta chains are replaced by gamma chains.
Carbon-dioxide affinity does not explain the characteristic left shift of the HbF oxygen-dissociation curve.
key_expl: HbF contains gamma rather than beta chains. Gamma chains interact less strongly with 2,3-BPG, so HbF has greater oxygen affinity and a left-shifted dissociation curve, promoting maternal-to-fetal oxygen transfer.
objective: Connect the high oxygen affinity of fetal hemoglobin to reduced 2,3-BPG binding by gamma globin chains.
